colophon: Thus ends the Shiva Tandava Stotram composed by Sri Ravana.

lines.1: From the forest of his matted hair a stream of water pours, and the ground it washes is made holy;
lines.2: around his neck hangs a towering garland of serpents;
lines.3: his damaru drum sounds ḍamaḍ ḍamaḍ ḍamaḍ ḍaman:
lines.4: so Shiva danced the fierce Tandava. May Shiva spread blessings over us.
lines.5: The river of the gods whirls and wanders in the cauldron of his matted locks,
lines.6: and her restless waves, like creepers, shine upon his head;
lines.7: on the plate of his forehead a fire blazes, dhagad dhagad dhagaj;
lines.8: he wears the young moon as his crest. In him may my delight be, every moment.
lines.9: He is the companion of the play of the Mountain King's daughter, and her beauty;
lines.10: his heart rejoices in the glittering expanse of all the horizons;
lines.11: the stream of his merciful glances holds back troubles too heavy to bear.
lines.12: In that sky-clad one, now and then, may my mind find its delight.
lines.13: The serpents in his matted hair glow tawny, and the gems on their flickering hoods shine,
lines.14: smearing the faces of the directions, the brides of space, as with liquid saffron;
lines.15: he is wrapped in a glistening upper cloth, the hide of a rut-blinded elephant.
lines.16: In the Lord of beings may my mind hold a wonderful joy.
lines.17: Indra the thousand-eyed and all the gods bow their crowned heads to him,
lines.18: and the pollen falling from their flowers turns his footstool grey;
lines.19: his matted locks are bound up with a garland of the serpent king.
lines.20: May he whose crest is the moon, friend of the chakora bird, bring prosperity that lasts.
lines.21: With sparks from the fire that burns on the broad courtyard of his forehead
lines.22: he swallowed the five-arrowed god of love; the lord of the gods bows to him;
lines.23: his crest shines with the slender crescent of the nectar-rayed moon.
lines.24: May that head, the great skull-bearer's, with its matted hair, bring us wealth.
lines.25: On the fearsome plate of his forehead blazes, dhagad dhagad dhagaj, a fire
lines.26: to which he offered up the fierce five-arrowed god of love;
lines.27: he alone is the artist who paints the ornamental lines on the breasts
lines.28: of the Mountain King's daughter. On the three-eyed one my thought is fixed.
lines.29: Dark as a mass of new rain clouds, thick and impenetrable,
lines.30: his throat is black as the night of the new moon;
lines.31: bearing the river of the gods, wearing the elephant's hide, may he spread
lines.32: prosperity, lovely with the moon, he who carries the burden of the world.
lines.33: Glowing with the darkness of blue lotuses in full and spreading bloom,
lines.34: his neck is bound with the dark luster of his throat, like a hanging stem.
lines.35: The cutter-off of Kama, of Tripura, of worldly existence, of the sacrifice,
lines.36: of the elephant demon and of Andhaka, the cutter-off of Death himself: him I worship.
lines.37: From the blossom-cluster of the arts of Sarvamangala, the goddess without pride,
lines.38: he is the bee that sips the sweetness of the flowing nectar.
lines.39: The ender of Kama, ender of Tripura, ender of worldly existence, ender of the sacrifice,
lines.40: ender of the elephant demon and of Andhaka, the ender of Death himself: him I worship.
lines.41: Victory to him! From the hissing breath of the serpents that whirl in vast circles,
lines.42: the fire on his fearsome forehead flares out in spreading waves;
lines.43: dhimid dhimid dhimi sounds the mighty, auspicious mridanga drum,
lines.44: and to its rolling beat Shiva performs his fierce Tandava.
lines.45: Between a stone and a splendid bed, between a serpent and a string of pearls,
lines.46: between the costliest jewel and a clod of earth, between friend and foe,
lines.47: between a blade of grass and lotus eyes, between common people and the king of the earth,
lines.48: keeping my mind even: when will I worship Sadashiva?
lines.49: When, dwelling in a hollow of the thickets by the river of the gods,
lines.50: free of evil thoughts, always holding my folded hands above my head,
lines.51: my restless eyes released, intent on the one with the eye in his forehead,
lines.52: chanting the mantra "Shiva," shall I live happy always?
lines.53: This supreme hymn of hymns, spoken here:
lines.54: whoever reads it, remembers it, recites it every day is made pure for ever,
lines.55: and soon gains true devotion to Hara, the Guru; there is no other way.
lines.56: For embodied beings, thinking on Shankara frees them from delusion.
lines.57: At the close of worship, this song of the Ten-Faced One:
lines.58: whoever, devoted to the worship of Shambhu, recites it in the evening hour of pradosha,
lines.59: to him, steady, with chariots, lordly elephants and horses,
